title: The shape of an idea
subtitle: A short guide to turning complexity into understanding
creator: Palim
description: An illustrative reading edition demonstrating diagrams, comparisons, source notes and readable technical explanations.

chapters.title: Start with a question
chapters.markdown:
A useful explanation begins with something the reader wants to understand. It does not begin with a list of everything the author knows.

Imagine a small publishing tool. Your agent understands the source material. A publisher turns that explanation into a book. A delivery service carries the finished file to your reader.

![A small publishing journey](figure:journey)

The boundaries matter. The publisher does not need access to your whole repository. The delivery service does not need to rewrite your book. Each part does one necessary job.

## The question worth asking

Instead of asking for a comprehensive overview, ask: **What should I be able to explain after reading this?**

For an architecture guide, that might be who owns each fact, how one request travels through the system, and what changes when a dependency fails.

chapters.title: Choose the form that explains
chapters.markdown:
A diagram is useful when its relationships answer a question. A chart is useful when comparing positions makes real values easier to understand. Neither is improved by adding decoration that hides the point.

| Reader question | Useful form |
| --- | --- |
| What happens next? | A sequence |
| What depends on what? | A relationship diagram |
| What do we gain or give up? | A comparison |

![An explicitly hypothetical comparison](figure:example-bars)

These numbers are **invented demonstration values**, not a measurement of learning or product performance. In a real book, the author would supply the actual data, units, period and source.

## Preserve the explanation

Keep ordinary words as text. Put a caption beside the figure. Make the point understandable even when the reader cannot distinguish colours.

chapters.title: Some things should stay unchanged
chapters.markdown:
Creating a new book and forwarding an existing book are different operations.

When somebody supplies an EPUB and asks to send it unchanged, there is nothing to author. The original file should remain the original file.

```text
uploaded bytes
  → integrity check
  → email attachment
```

The attachment can be compared with the upload using a SHA-256 checksum. Matching checksums establish byte identity at that boundary. They do not establish what a receiving service later converts, displays or stores.

That distinction is the whole idea: make new explanations carefully, and leave existing books alone.
